problem: Product analytics tools were closed, expensive and sent user data to third parties; engineers wanted an open source self-hostable one.
business_model: Open source with usage-based cloud pricing

technical_complexity.rationale: Event ingestion and analytics at scale with self-hosting; MVP built in about four weeks.

defensibility.rationale: Open source gives trust but is forkable; value grew from breadth of bundled products and data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not stop PostHog, which grew past them in valuation breadth by 2025.

market_need_then: Privacy rules such as GDPR and engineer preference for self-hosted tooling; founders launched on Hacker News in February 2020 (282 points).

branding.name_origin: Named after a hedgehog, per a short remark in PostHog's hiring post.

identity.mascot_or_character: Max the hedgehog, drawn by designer Lottie Coxon (2021)

branding.community_and_virality: Plushies, outfit variants of Max and a handbook brand policy (company sources); a blog calls its brand strategy weird.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive mascot and tone that the company itself invests in; no independent measurement of its effect.

pivots.from: Several early product ideas during YC
pivots.why: YC feedback and a Hacker News launch deadline of February 20, 2020

outcome_analysis: PostHog pivoted during YC W20 to open source product analytics, launched on Hacker News in February 2020 and raised a seed and a GV led $9M Series A the same year. It stayed lean (the company says it is default alive), then raised a $70M Series D at $920M in June 2025 and a reported $75M at $1.4B in September 2025 by broadening into a bundled developer platform.
notes: Seed amount reported as $3M, $3.025M and $3.2M; seed and Series A dates differ between press release and handbook. Series B reportedly about $15M in 2021 (single snippet, unverified, so amount null). Series C amount about $10M from the company blog with no date or investors. Series E ($75M at $1.4B, Peak XV, September 2025) is from aggregator snippets only and flagged estimated. Founder prior employers not found. Conflict resolved to the company blog: seed $3M closed 2020-03 and Series A $9M closed 2020-07 (GV lead), with the $12M total announced 2020-12-17 in the BusinessWire release. Series B of $15M announced 2021-06-10 (BusinessWire, lead YC Continuity Fund with GV); PostHog's media page dates it 2021-03, conflicting with the June announcement. Series C amount about $10M remains undated.
